original: This bottle I bought to put a scant teaspoon into my home made ice cream to keep it from forming ice crystals after storing in the freezer. I just bought a Cuisinart Ice Cream Machine and followed a simple recipe for chocolate ice cream, but I wanted to make sure that it would not become hard and full of ice crystals once I stored it in the freezer, so I did some research online and glycerin is one of several ways to keep ice cream creamy. It only takes a teaspoon in the recipe and the other thing about glycerin is that it is sweet, so it blends in well with an ice cream recipe. My ice cream turned out great and it is smooth and creamy after being in the freezer. Now, this is not my first use of glycerin as I have used a small amount in water to spray in my hair. Especially on really humid days when my naturally curly hair turns into a frizz-ball, spraying my hair with a 10 parts water, 1 part glycerin (or even less glycerin, depending) keeps my hair from frizzing out so bad. For me, in ice cream or in my hair, glycerin works great!
sampled: This was a verified purchase for me, and I gave the glycerin a 5.0 rating. I had recently purchased a Cuisinart Ice Cream Machine and bought this bottle specifically to add glycerin to homemade ice cream, mainly because I wanted to reduce ice crystal formation once the ice cream went into freezer storage. I made chocolate ice cream from a simple recipe and used a scant teaspoon, which is about a teaspoon, in the batch. The result after freezer storage was smooth and creamy, not icy in the way I was trying to avoid. The sweetness of glycerin also fit well in the ice cream, so it did not feel out of place for that use. For me, it works well for both ice cream and hair use, so the bottle feels practical rather than like a single-purpose purchase.
